footnotes.text: The references to services are those services which have allocations in Article 5.

Equality of right to operate when a band is allocated in different Regions to different services of the same category is established in No. 4.8; limits concerning inter-Regional interference in ITU-R Recommendations should, as far as practicable, be observed.

In addition to the limits given in Table 21-4, in the band 18.6-18.8 GHz ... the power flux-density across the 200 MHz band 18.6-18.8 GHz produced at the surface of the Earth by emissions from a space station under assumed free-space propagation conditions shall not exceed −95 dB(W/m2), except for less than 5% of time, when the limit may be exceeded by up to 3 dB. The provisions of No. 21.17 do not apply in this band. (WRC-2000)

Values derived on the basis of protecting the fixed service using line-of-sight techniques. Where tropospheric-scatter fixed service operates ... interference power at the receiver input of the fixed-service station does not exceed −168 dBW in any 4 kHz band.
Resolution 903 (Rev.WRC-19) shall apply. (WRC-19)

The values given in this table entry shall apply to emissions of space stations of non-geostationary satellites in systems operating with 99 or fewer satellites. Further study ... necessary in order to apply them to systems operating with 100 or more satellites. (WRC-2000)
These values are applicable where this band is shared with equal rights with meteorological aids service.

The function X is defined as a function of the number, N, of satellites in the non-geostationary satellite constellation in the fixed-satellite service and Nv: X = 0 dB for N ≤ 50; X = (5/119)(N − 50) dB for 50 < N ≤ 288; X = (1/69)(N + 402) dB for 288 < N ≤ 999; X = max {20.3; 10 log10(Nv)} dB for 1 000 ≤ N ≤ 6 000; X = 10 log10(Nv) + 1 dB for N > 6 000. Nv is the maximum number of visible space stations (minimum elevation 0 degrees) from any location within the service area of the non-GSO system [definition footnoted: Nv = Max(Nv(j = 0,1,2...)) with Nv(j) = Max(Nv(j(t)), Nv(j(t − 1)))]. In the band 18.8-19.3 GHz these limits apply to emissions of any space station in a non-GSO system in the FSS for which complete coordination or notification information has been received by the BR since 17 November 1995 and which was not operational by that date, and in the inter-satellite service. (WRC-23)
footnotes.doubt: X formulas are printed as stacked fractions: 5 over 119 times (N−50); 1 over 69 times (N+402). The text layer garbles them; read from the image.

footnotes.text: These limits apply to emissions of a space station in the meteorological-satellite service and of a geostationary satellite in the fixed-satellite and inter-satellite services. They also apply to emissions of any space station in a non-GSO system in the FSS in the band 18.8-19.3 GHz for which complete coordination or notification information has been received by the BR by 17 November 1995, or which was in operation by that date. (WRC-23)

These limits also apply to FSS space stations using highly-inclined orbits having an apogee altitude greater than 18 000 km and an orbital inclination between 35° and 145° in the band 17.7-19.7 GHz to which Resolution 147 (WRC-07) applies. (WRC-07)

These limits apply to all space stations that use highly-inclined orbits having an apogee altitude greater than 18 000 km and an orbital inclination between 35° and 145° in the band 17.7-19.7 GHz in the FSS and that are not covered by Resolution 147 (WRC-07), and for which complete coordination or notification information was received by the BR after 16 November 2007, and in the inter-satellite service. (WRC-23)
These power flux-density limits are subject to review by ITU-R and shall apply until they are revised by a competent world radiocommunication conference.

The pfd values given for EESS (active) are mean pfd values: pfd(δ) = P + 10log(τ) + 10log(PRF) − 30 − 10log(Bc) + Gt(δ) − 10log(4πd²(δ)); P RF peak power at antenna input (dBW), τ SAR pulse length (μs), PRF pulse repetition frequency (kHz), δ elevation angle of the SAR satellite above ground (°), Bc SAR emission bandwidth (MHz), Gt(δ) transmit gain (dBi), d(δ) distance (m). (WRC-15)
These values are also based on sharing with the Earth exploration-satellite (active) and space research services. (WRC-15)

During the launch and near-Earth operational phase of deep-space facilities, non-geostationary satellite systems in the space research service shall not exceed: −115 dB(W/m2) for δ < 5°; −115 + 0.5 (δ – 5) dB(W/m2) for 5° ≤ δ ≤ 25°; −105 dB(W/m2) for δ > 25°; in any 1 MHz band. (WRC-2000)
(SUP - WRC-03)

In 37.5-40 GHz and 40.5-42.5 GHz the pfd from any FSS satellite should be no greater than the level(s) required to meet the FSS link availability and performance objectives ...; in any case the levels shall not exceed the applicable pfd limits in Table 21-4. (WRC-03)

The value of Y is defined as Y = 0 for max(NN, NS) ≤ 2; Y = 5 log(max(NN, NS)) for max(NN, NS) > 2, where NN (NS) is the maximum number of space stations in a system simultaneously transmitting co-frequency in the FSS in the Northern (Southern) Hemisphere. Two space stations simultaneously transmitting during short-duration handover count as one satellite. (WRC-03)
footnotes.doubt: The text layer loses the '>' in 'max(NN, NS) > 2'; the image shows '> 2'.

footnotes.text: The applicability of these limits may need to be reviewed by a future competent conference if the number of co-frequency non-geostationary systems brought into use and simultaneously operating in the same hemisphere is greater than five. (WRC-03)
These limits apply to non-geostationary FSS space stations employing an orbit with an inclination angle between 35° and 145° and apogee altitude greater than 18 000 km. (WRC-03)
These limits apply to non-geostationary FSS space stations that are not covered by No. 21.16.17. (WRC-03)

The methodology included in Annex 2 to Resolution 679 (WRC-23) shall be applied to calculate the pfd produced at the surface of the Earth by emissions from a non-geostationary-satellite space station transmitting in the frequency band 27.5-30.0 GHz. (WRC-23)
The limits given in Table 21-4 may be exceeded on the territory of any country whose administration has so agreed. (Provision following the table, not a table footnote.)
